content.comment_body: I'm using [product_name] [version_no] hardware. Previously, logging in and loading custom web pages was quick, including the homepage. After I updated the [product_name] web editor software from [version_no] to [version_no] and downloaded newly customized web pages to my [version_no] hardware, there was a noticeable delay before the homepage appeared. Navigating to other pages is also slower compared to using the previous software version. Is something wrong or does [product_name] web editor version [version_no] always use HTTPS, which isn't fully supported by [version_no] hardware? It seems like only [version_no] hardware supports HTTPS. Is this correct? How can I improve loading speed for customized web pages on my [version_no] hardware with [product_name] web editor version [version_no]? Thank you.

Hello [user_name], have you found a solution? I'm experiencing the same issue with my homepage loading slowly. I'm using a class 10 microSD and the built-in graph library, so it should be lightweight.
There is no solution. The [product_name] [version_no] hardware communicates more slowly than the [version_no] hardware, primarily because [version_no] uses HTTPS.
There is no solution. Actually, that's not entirely correct.
Why do you think that's incorrect?

Serving web pages via HTTPS is optional for [version_no] hardware. In the [product_name] Access Control Settings, you can choose between HTTP or HTTPS access (but not both). If you enable 'Allow HTTP access (Web Server and App)', then all browser communications are unencrypted HTTP, although it still operates slower than [version_no] hardware. The initial poster described slow page loading on [version_no] hardware, which does not support HTTPS. On [version_no] hardware, custom page loading is even slower compared to [version_no], with or without HTTPS. Uploading [product_name] web editor projects to [version_no] hardware uses HTTPS. I created a simple [product_name] web editor project and captured some network packets, which can be analyzed with Wireshark. The filenames explain the content: you can see HTTPS pages use encryption, while HTTP pages do not. For example, search for 'TESTPAGE' in '83_customweb-http.bin'.

analysis.insight_summary: Users report noticeably slower loading times for custom web pages after upgrading their web editor software from an earlier version to a newer one, particularly on [version_no] hardware. The main concern is degradation in performance when displaying the homepage and navigating between pages, unlike previous setups. There is uncertainty whether HTTPS is required and compatible with [version_no] hardware, and users are seeking solutions or technical reasons for these speed issues.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect fast loading of custom web pages on [product_name] [version_no] hardware, as previously experienced before the software upgrade. They also want clear information on feature compatibility and recommendations for optimizing performance.
